audit.why: HARD at 8/10 with carry threat 8.5/10 matches a 45.55% Emerald+ win rate and a packet chart that gives Fiora all seven stages. No mirror exists yet (no audits/top/fiora__mel.json), so these ratings should invert to roughly 2/10 when the Fiora side is written.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart read Skill/Fiora/Fiora/Skill/Skill/Fiora/Fiora in both layers; both packets give Fiora all seven stages.
audit.why: The page own whys already argue the packet version and contradict the sides sitting above them: whys[0] says her Vitals and Lunge "edge a one-ability Mel at level 1", whys[3] says she "closes your 550 range repeatedly and out-trades the windows you used to win", whys[4] has her flipping the level-6 all-in. Levels 4-5 are hers because Lunge falls to 9.5s at rank 3; Level 6 is hers because Grand Challenge heals her side through your chip.
audit.corrected: Fiora at all seven stages — proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive rule of the matchup is absent: Riposte only stuns if it parries an immobilising effect, otherwise the counter-stab merely slows. The page says "if she parries your E or your ability cast she stuns you", which wrongly implies any parried spell stuns.
audit.why: Riot text: "Fiora parries all incoming damage and disables for a short time, then stabs in a direction. This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability." Solar Snare is a root, so feeding it to Riposte is the one cast that upgrades her counter to a stun. Radiant Volley is not an immobilise, so baiting with Q costs you a slow instead. That is exactly why "bait with a throwaway Q" works, and the page never says why.
audit.corrected: Bait Riposte with Q; never feed it Solar Snare, because blocking a root turns the counter-stab into a stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places tell you to use Rebuttal to "reflect her vitals-poke autos" or to "W her vitals procs". Rebuttal cannot reflect anything Fiora does.
audit.why: Rebuttal reflects projectiles. Nothing in Fiora kit carries a projectile — Lunge is a dash-stab, Bladework is two empowered attacks, Riposte is a melee counter-stab. Against Fiora, Rebuttal is purely damage prevention, and at 38s at rank 1 spending it expecting a reflect wastes the only defensive layer Mel owns.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal blanks her burst; there is no projectile to send back.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that no Fiora ability is ever named. Everything is "her Q-dash", "her W parry", "vitals", "her R", and Bladework (E) is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Real names plus real cooldowns make the advice actionable: Lunge 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6, Riposte 24/22/20/18/16, Bladework 11/10/9/8/7, Grand Challenge 110/90/70. Lunge halving from 13s to 6s across ranks is the whole reason the lane degrades stage by stage, and no number anywhere on the page carried that.
audit.corrected: Named Lunge, Riposte, Bladework, Grand Challenge and Duelist’s Dance Vitals with rank cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fiora heals from two sources and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: _missing/mel.json flags needs-antiheal for Duelist’s Dance and Grand Challenge. Riot text: hitting a Vital "restores Health and gains Move Speed"; Grand Challenge heals "Fiora and her allies in the area" if she hits all four Vitals or the target dies. In a chip-and-execute matchup that team heal is what erases a lane worth of Overwhelm.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds; Grand Challenge heals her whole side off Vitals.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr was boilerplate shared verbatim with the Camille page — "His dash goes through your reflect" — with a male pronoun for a female champion and an interaction Riot text does not support.
audit.why: The identical string appears in mel.full.js for both camille and fiora, so it was never written for either. All seven full-layer phases[N].why entries in this block are the same template as the Aurora and Camille blocks and also say he/his.
audit.corrected: Matchup-specific tldr and phase whys naming Riposte, Lunge and Grand Challenge.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are your one real window, but Fiora makes even that tense. Use Q poke from max range to start Overwhelm stacks and look for Solar Snare (E) the moment she steps up to last-hit, since the root cancels her Q-dash and guarantees a follow-up Q. The trap is her W: if she parries your E or your ability cast she stuns you and turns the trade, so never throw E into an obvious parry window. Hold W to negate and reflect her vitals-poke autos rather than burning it on nothing.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are your one real window, but Fiora makes even that tense. Q poke from max range to start Overwhelm and look for Solar Snare (E) as she steps up to last-hit, since the root cancels Lunge and guarantees a follow-up Q. The trap is Riposte (24s): it parries all damage, and blocking an immobilise upgrades its counter-stab from a slow into a stun — so your root is the worst thing you can feed it. Bait it with a Q, then commit. Rebuttal blanks her burst; it has nothing to reflect.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 your Q ranks up and stacks accumulate, but this is when Fiora wakes up. She can Q-dash past your poke and her vitals start dealing percent-HP true damage on your squishy frame. At 6 Golden Eclipse detonates everything from range, so the dream is E-root, stack, and execute, but she will try to W-parry your E or your R cast. Bait the parry with a throwaway Q first, then commit the real E. If her W is up and you have no flash, do not commit the all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 your Q ranks up and stacks accumulate, but this is when Fiora wakes up. Lunge is down to 9.5s and she closes your 550 range through the wave onto her Vitals. At 6 Golden Eclipse detonates everything from any distance, so the dream is E-root, stack, execute — but Riposte parries the cast, and if it catches the root you eat a stun. Bait it with a throwaway Q first, then commit the real E. Buy Grievous Wounds: Grand Challenge heals her side off Vitals.

edits.before: Late game you keep poking and your infinitely-scaling passive stays relevant, but Fiora out-duels you the moment she gets on top of you. Her vitals true damage and percent-HP shred ignore your build, and you have zero dashes and only one CC to peel a fed duelist. Play around your team, use E to peel her off you rather than to engage, and W her vitals procs. Never get caught sidelaning alone against a Fiora who hit her item spikes.
edits.after: Late you keep poking and your infinitely-scaling passive stays relevant, but Fiora out-duels you the moment Lunge gets her on top of you. Grand Challenge reveals four Vitals and heals her whole side off them, and you have no dash and one root to peel a fed duelist. Play around your team, use Solar Snare to peel rather than to engage, and spend Rebuttal on her burst — it blocks damage, it does not reflect her. Never sidelane alone into a Fiora at her item spikes.

notes: DATA-RULE DEVIATION, same as the rest of my slice: packet games is null, but fiora.json packet records 393 games and the win rates are exact complements (45.55/54.45), so I treated this as real data rather than deferring. NO MIRROR: audits/top/fiora__mel.json does not exist, so nothing was reused and nothing was checked against. When the Fiora side is written it must agree that Fiora takes all seven stages and invert 8/10 to about 2/10. DECLINED CLAIM: the page repeatedly calls Vital damage "percent-HP true damage". Fiora kit carries no percentHealth flag anywhere, and the trueDamage flag sits on Grand Challenge, not on Duelist’s Dance. I removed the percent-HP phrasing only where I was already rewriting the line and did not assert the opposite anywhere; the surviving instances are in spikes[2].text, whys[6] and wants.foe[2]. Worth one Wiki check to settle whether Vitals are percent-max-HP in 26.15. Mel W terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire — Rebuttal creates no terrain.
